MATERIAL GUIDE · HOMEOWNER GUIDE

Metal, Tile or Shingle Roofing? A Florida Homeowner’s Comparison

A practical comparison of metal, tile and asphalt shingle roofing for Florida homes, including structural fit, coastal exposure, maintenance and estimates.

Near Shore Roofing LLC · Published October 14, 2026 · 2 min read

IN THIS GUIDE

Start with the house and the siteMetal: specify the whole assemblyTile: look beneath the visible surfaceShingles: compare products and installation detailsReflectivity is a product propertyMake the final comparison on equal terms

Start with the house and the site

The best roof material for a property depends on more than its appearance. Roof slope, the supporting structure, nearby salt exposure, drainage, and the homeowner’s maintenance expectations all matter. Before narrowing the color palette, ask which systems are suitable for the roof you have and what changes would be required to install them correctly.

Metal: specify the whole assembly

A metal roof’s clean lines can suit many coastal homes. Compare the proposed metal, finish, panel profile, attachment method, and flashing details. For properties near salt water, ask the manufacturer’s requirements for that exposure and the limitations of the specific warranty. Exposed fasteners and concealed-fastener systems have different details to maintain. Do not assume that every metal product has the same corrosion resistance or maintenance needs.

Tile: look beneath the visible surface

Tile offers a distinctive profile, but the waterproofing beneath the tiles deserves careful evaluation. Broken tiles and aging underlayment are different issues. A change from another roofing material may require evaluation of structural support. Ask how valleys, penetrations, roof edges, and underlayment will be handled. Avoid walking on tile yourself; foot traffic can damage tiles and create a fall risk.

Shingles: compare products and installation details

Asphalt shingles come in varied profiles and colors. Ask which product is proposed and which starter, underlayment, ventilation, and edge components accompany it. An estimate should describe installation requirements and the condition of the deck. A broad lifespan claim is less useful than a clear specification and an explanation of maintenance expectations.

Reflectivity is a product property

A material category alone does not determine energy performance. Surface reflectance, thermal emittance, roof construction, insulation, and climate all influence results. The U.S. Department of Energy explains that cool-roof products are available across several roofing categories. Ask for product data and avoid treating a roof replacement as a guaranteed utility-bill reduction.

Make the final comparison on equal terms

Request estimates with comparable removal, decking allowances, protective layers, flashings, cleanup, and warranty documentation. Discuss the appearance alongside the practical constraints. Near Shore Roofing lists metal, tile, and shingle roofing services; a property-specific conversation can help narrow the options.
